finding.title: Programmatic dialog close may be reported as a user dismissal
finding.message: closeDialog sets d.closing for the duration of body.Close() and clears it immediately afterwards. If Cogent delivers the close event to the body's OnClose handler asynchronously, the handler sees closing == false. It then marks the dialog dismissed and calls the model's Dismiss callback even though the model closed it. The handler also sets d.body = nil unconditionally, which could clobber a newly prepared body.
finding.suggestion: Make the OnClose handler identify its own body, for example by comparing `d.body` to the body it was created for and ignoring stale closes. Track programmatic closes per body instead of with a shared flag that is reset right after Close(). Confirm in Cogent whether Close() runs OnClose synchronously.
finding.evidence:
d.closing = true
	tree.MoveToParent(d.host, r.widget)
	d.host.SetScene(r.widget.AsWidget().Scene)
	body.Close()
	d.body = nil
	d.active = false
	d.closing = false

finding.title: Unchecked type assertion and shallow scene reassignment when re-parenting widgets
finding.message: The unchecked type assertion `p.parent.(core.Widget)` panics if `childHost` ever returns a `tree.Node` that is not a `core.Widget`. `plan.parent` is typed `tree.Node`, so the compiler does not guarantee the assertion holds. `SetScene` is also applied only to the moved widget, not its descendants. If `MoveToParent` does not propagate the scene, nested widgets keep the parking frame's scene.
finding.suggestion: Use a checked assertion, for example `if pw, ok := p.parent.(core.Widget); ok { p.r.widget.AsWidget().SetScene(pw.AsWidget().Scene) }`. Also confirm that descendants of the moved widget are re-scened, for example by walking the subtree.

discarded.reason: refuted by anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5: The panic and the shallow scene update are both speculative. Every plan.parent is either the core.Widget root parent or a host returned by childHost, which holds widget children and so is a widget in practice. The parking frame is created under the same managed parent, so retained descendants already share the same Scene. The extra SetScene call is a harmless safeguard, not a real defect.
